title: Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter
principle: Asking for wireframes is much faster, and it keeps Claude focused on higher-level structure instead of visuals. Use this to try many different ideas quickly before committing to look-and-feel.
procedure: When fidelity doesn’t matter, explicitly ask for wireframes only.
Escalate fidelity only after hierarchy and flow feel right.
examplePrompts: Wireframe only—no visual styling. Gray boxes, labels, and hierarchy. Give me 5 structural alternatives for this flow so I can compare layout ideas quickly.
Build a greyscale wireframe only—no brand color, no imagery, no polish. Same IA and hierarchy as the brief. Stop and show me before any visual pass.
tips: Speed comes from skipping premature visual decisions.
Structure-first prevents Claude from locking onto a favorite aesthetic early.
Nate uses Claude Design daily for wireframing early ideas and generating many flow versions for feedback.
Pairs with sketch-what-you-cant-describe when you already have paper boxes.

antiPatterns: Jumping to polished visuals while structure is still mush.
Letting early aesthetic defaults lock the layout.
Asking for high-fidelity chrome before the information hierarchy is set.
checklist: Fresh pass confirms the prompt constraints were followed.
promptWhy: Gray-box constraint keeps the model on hierarchy, not favorite aesthetics.
Greyscale gate stops the model from burning tokens on chrome before structure is right.

useWhen: The current discover task needs this specific principle: Asking for wireframes is much faster, and it keeps Claude focused on higher-level structure instead of visuals. Use this to try many different ideas quickly before committing to look-and-feel.
avoidWhen: Jumping to polished visuals while structure is still mush.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
1. When fidelity doesn’t matter, explicitly ask for wireframes only.
2. Compare multiple structural directions quickly.
3. Lock structure before high-fidelity visuals.
4. Escalate fidelity only after hierarchy and flow feel right.
acceptance: Show the before/after artifact and explain how “Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter” improves the named user task.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
